subsections.subsection_title: 2. Differential Diagnosis of Chronic Liver Disease (CLD)

items.text: Chronic hepatic venous outflow obstruction (Budd–Chiari syndrome)
Chronic hepatitis D in patients with hepatitis B
hepatic infiltration by lymphoma (may coexist with or complicate CLD)
chronic biliary injury or stricture following trauma or surgery
Infection: spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, pneumonia, UTI, sepsis

subsections.subsection_title: 4. Signs and Symptoms of Chronic Liver Disease (CLD)

items.text: Dark urine and pale stools (in cholestasis).
Reduced libido, amenorrhoea or erectile dysfunction.
Confusion or altered sleep pattern (hepatic encephalopathy).
Hepatomegaly or a small, shrunken liver.
Right upper quadrant tenderness in selected cases.

subsections.subsection_title: 5. Complications of Obstructive Jaundice and Causes

items.text: Fat-soluble vitamin deficiency (A, D, E, K)
Carcinoma of the head of pancreas
Lymph node compression at the porta hepatis
acute hepatic congestion due to right-sided heart failure
Breastfeeding-associated jaundice due to inadequate intake
Haemolytic disease of the newborn: Rh, ABO incompatibility
Sickle cell disease and other haemolytic anaemias
Hepatitis A, B, C and E
Haemolytic disorders: autoimmune haemolytic anaemia, G6PD-related haemolysis
Portal hypertension: cirrhosis, portal vein thrombosis, schistosomiasis
Congestive: right-sided heart failure, splenic vein thrombosis
Infiltrative/storage: Gaucher disease, Niemann–Pick disease, amyloidosis, sarcoidosis
Autoimmune/inflammatory: SLE, rheumatoid arthritis with Felty syndrome
Others: splenic cysts, splenic tumours, haemolytic disease of the newborn
Faecal impaction / functional distension (mnemonic variants exist)

blocks.text: Definition: Generalised severe oedema involving subcutaneous tissues, often with ascites and/or pleural effusions.
